issues.description: Log buffering, crash detection, and OTLP replay are complected across four call sites with no single owner of the lifecycle.
issues.detail: The buffer's identity (early_log_handler), its time semantics (start at _run_job_task, stop in init_recording, or replay in _on_cleanup), and its destination (an OTLP handler discovered by isinstance scan of the root logger) are spread across job.py, job_proc_lazy_main.py, and traces.py. No one place describes the state machine. COMPLECTED.

issues.description: Replay target is found by scanning root logger handlers for a LoggingHandler instance instead of holding the reference as a value.
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer iterates logging.getLogger().handlers looking for the first LoggingHandler. That couples replay to global mutable state set up elsewhere by _setup_cloud_tracer, with no guarantee of identity. Pass the handler in as data, or hold the reference returned by setup. PLACE-ORIENTED.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler buffer is unbounded and uses no synchronization despite logging from arbitrary threads.
issues.detail: logging handlers may be called from any thread; list.append is mostly safe in CPython but the buffer has no cap. A crash loop or a chatty subsystem before connect() can grow buffer without bound and then be replayed to OTLP. Bound the buffer (ring) and state the policy explicitly. ESSENTIAL-COMPLEXITY missed.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry now mutates root logger handlers as a side effect of shutdown, complecting telemetry teardown with global logging state.
issues.detail: The fix removes every LoggingHandler from the root logger before force_flush to avoid a deadlock. That entangles telemetry shutdown with whatever else the application attached. Track the handler installed by _setup_cloud_tracer as a value and remove only that one, instead of scanning and removing by type. COMPLECTED.

issues.description: init_recording silently stops buffering when recording is already initialized or url is not cloud, hiding a meaningful state transition.
issues.detail: The early-return branch now also calls _stop_log_buffering with no replay. That means buffered crash logs are dropped on a path that looks like a no-op guard. Make the discard explicit, or push the buffering decision into one function that names both outcomes. EASY-NOT-SIMPLE.

issues.description: Removing -n auto and test_plugin_google_stt.py from unit-tests is unexplained and unrelated to the crash-log feature.
issues.detail: Two test infrastructure changes are folded into a feature PR with no note: serial pytest execution and excluding a plugin test. If these are flaky-test workarounds, name them; if they are required for the feature, say so. Otherwise they should ship separately. Mixing concerns in the diff is its own form of complecting.

review.summary: The feature adds a real capability — capturing logs before init_recording so crash diagnostics survive — but the implementation spreads buffer lifecycle across three modules and relies on isinstance scans of the global root logger to find both the source and destination of replay. The state machine (start, stop-without-replay, replay, drop) has four outcomes and no single function names them. Telemetry shutdown now mutates the root logger as a side effect, which is a separate complecting that will outlive this PR. Hold the OTLP handler and the buffer as values owned by one component, bound the buffer, and split the unrelated test-runner changes into their own PR.
